::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 30th [1867]  
**From:** Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MSS. Wilberforce c. 16 ff64-5
:::

[My Lord](people/person_1512.qmd),
Allow me to express my gratitude for the kindness of your invitation and of the arrangement for the journey. I must however beg to decline it until another year when I hope I may have the pleasure of making your [daughter](people/person_1218.qmd)’s acquaintance under more cheerful circumstances.

I cannot at present feel inclined to enter on a large party, nor to leave my [mother](people/person_1606.qmd), and I should be much obliged if you would allow me to consider the visit as deferred until some future time.[^1]

With many thanks for your kindness
Yours very respectfully 
Charlotte M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: CMY had been in Devon in October, returning on 12 November 1867. This excuse to Bishop Wilberforce may mark the beginning of her mother’s decline.
